name: Stars and bars
formula: x_1 + \cdots + x_k = n,\ x_i \ge 0: \ \binom{n + k - 1}{k - 1} \qquad x_i \ge 1: \ \binom{n - 1}{k - 1}
whenToUse: Distribute identical objects into distinct boxes, count nonnegative integer solutions to a sum, or choose with repetition allowed.
example: $x + y + z = 10$ has $\binom{12}{2} = 66$ nonnegative solutions and $\binom{9}{2} = 36$ positive ones. Buying $10$ donuts from $3$ flavours is the same as the first count.
pitfall: It only works for IDENTICAL objects in DISTINCT boxes. For a lower bound like $x \ge 2$, substitute $x' = x - 2$ first; upper bounds need inclusion-exclusion.
derivation: Line up $n$ stars and $k - 1$ bars. Each arrangement splits the stars into $k$ groups, one per variable, and choosing the bar positions among $n + k - 1$ spots gives the count.
